newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's king says politician's death "not in vain".
newsitem.headline: Spain's king says politician's death "not in vain".

text.p: King Juan Carlos told the Spanish people on Monday night that the death of Miguel Angel Blanco -- a young politician killed by Basque separatists -- "has not been in vain".
In a rare televised message to the nation, the king sought to reassure Spaniards, telling them he had "followed with great emotion the condemnation of terrorism throughout Spain".
In a taped message from the lawn of the royal palace, the king praised the widespread reaction to the brutal killing of Blanco, whose body was found on Saturday bound and bloodied.

"The Spanish have given an unsurpassable example of civility and unity. I would tell them that the death of Miguel Angel has not been in vain, and to continue fighting in this endless struggle for democracy, liberty and human rights," he said.

Blanco, 29, was killed after ETA rebels kidnapped him and demanded the government move about 500 ETA inmates to the Basque region before 4 p.m on Saturday. He was found with two gunshot wounds in his head shortly after the deadline and died 12 hours later.

His killing sparked an angry public outcry against the rebel group, and more than a million Spaniards took to the streets in central Madrid on Monday night in a demonstration led by Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar.
